Rook Fenner.narrative: I came down from the north shore years ago with a tarred boat and a north-shore accent the quay still laughs at, and I never went back. The outer shoals are my ground; I know their moods better than I know most men. Lyss keeps the soup stall by the tide steps, and our boy mends nets on the quay. We get by, though Ostrander Cormorant's share of the net hangs over me and the stone price keeps the quay poor.
values: paying what I owe when I can
goals: clear the net-share debt to Ostrander Cormorant
see the boy crew on a proper boat
keep the tarred boat sound another winter
learn the outer shoals' winter runs well enough to fish them safely alone
own a second net of his own, not hung on another man's share

memories.gist: I rowed down from the north shore with nothing but a tarred boat and a net, and the quay laughed at my accent.
The night the Surge came, I pulled Wick Gull's boat off the lower quay with a rope and my back.
Lyss and I set up the soup stall the week after we were married; she's run it ever since.
Ostrander Cormorant lent me a share of his net when mine tore, and I've not cleared it yet.
The boy mended his first net at seven and was quicker at it than me.

stances.why: A man who doesn't pay his debts is no better than a wrecker.
The shoals have fed us through lean times; I trust them more than the land.
The fish road is for runners and guards; my place is the boat.
The lower quay needs a wall, but I won't march for it.

Rook Fenner.secret: I've been setting aside a few marks in a jar behind the chimney to pay Cormorant before winter, and I've told no one, not even Lyss.
pastimes: mending and tarring his boat on the tide steps at low water
sitting at the inn with Wick Gull over a slow cup
walking the north cape shore at dusk to read the weather
Rook Fenner.calling: The outer shoals are my ground; I know their moods better than I know most men, and I would not trade the work for any other.

Lyss Fenner.narrative: I keep the soup and bread stall by the tide steps, up before the early boats and last to bank the fire. Rook fishes the outer shoals and our boy mends nets on the quay. I trade with Nia Gull and buy lamp oil from Nia Brine, and I know every debt on this quay by the way people order their soup. Sella Pike feeds half the quay on credit and owes Mira Sallow for medicines; I owe Sella a little myself, and it feels like the whole quay is living on promises.
values: a hot bowl for a cold morning
goals: keep the stall solvent through the lean season
see the boy settled with a crew
clear what I owe Sella Pike without hard words
learn to bake a bread worth selling on its own, not just alongside the soup
save enough marks to buy her own lamp oil in bulk before winter

relations.name: Rook Fenner
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He's a quiet man with a good boat; I'd have no one else.

relations.name: Rook Fenner the younger

relations.name: Sella Pike

relations.name: Mira Sallow
relations.label: neighbour

relations.name: Jory Pike

relations.note: Sella's boy, cheerful and always owing someone.

relations.name: Perrin Tallow
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She knows the price of everything, but she pays for the bread.

memories.gist: I set up the soup stall the week after Rook and I were married, with a pot borrowed from my mother.
The Surge took the lower quay and we fed the soaked families from the stall for three days.
Sella Pike gave me credit for a whole winter when Rook's boat was laid up, and I've not forgotten it.
The boy mended his first net at seven and was quicker at it than his father.
Nia Brine and I argued over the price of lamp oil and settled it over a bowl of soup.

stances.why: A cold fisherman is no good to anyone; the stall opens before dawn.
Credit is a kindness; I won't abuse it.
Sella's credit and the stone price have everyone owing everyone.
He wants Cormorant's boat, but the deep water took good men in the Surge.

pastimes: singing the old north-shore songs while she banks the stall's fire
trading gossip and news with Nia Gull over the soup pots
tending the little herb pots on her windowsill
Lyss Fenner.calling: A hot bowl for a cold morning is honest work, and I would keep this stall's name good as long as my hands can lift the ladle.

Rook Fenner the younger.narrative: I'm eleven and I mend nets on the quay, and I'm quick with a knot. Da fishes the outer shoals and Ma keeps the soup stall by the tide steps. Wick Cormorant and me play on the quay and I want to crew on his father's boat one day. The quay laughs at Da's accent, but I don't.
goals: mend a net as fast as Da
mend a whole net by himself before the season turns
learn the names of the outer shoals from Da

relations.name: Rook Fenner
relations.label: father

relations.name: Lyss Fenner

relations.name: Wick Cormorant
relations.label: friend

relations.name: Ostrander Cormorant
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: His boat is the best on the quay; I want to crew for him.

memories.gist: Da pulled Wick Gull's boat off the lower quay the night of the Surge, and I watched from the tide steps.
I mended my first net at seven and was quicker at it than Da.
Wick Cormorant and me raced our knots on the quay and he won, but I'm getting faster.

stances.why: I want to be a fisherman like Da, but on a bigger boat.
A good knot keeps the catch in and the boat safe.
The quay laughs at Da's north-shore accent, and I won't.

pastimes: playing tag and boat games on the quay with Wick Cormorant
practising knots on scraps of old net
watching the early boats come in from the tide steps
Rook Fenner the younger.calling: I want to crew on a proper boat one day, out past the harbour mouth where Da fishes.
